correctness.rationale: An H-fixed point of the geometric uniform matroid rank-r skeleton has barycentric coordinates constant on each permutation orbit. Its support gives exactly the weighted simplex L_r={S:sum w_i<=r}, not a quotient complex. With a chosen minimum orbit 1, z_S=d[1,S]=[S]-[1,dS] enters at weight w(S) because w_1<=w_i; y_S=[1,S] enters at w(S)+w_1. This is an invertible unitriangular filtration-respecting integral basis with d y_S=z_S and d z_S=0, yielding direct two-cell complexes and intervals [w(S),w(S)+w1) in degree |S|-1, no extension or torsion. Unique min orbit is fixed by the normalizer, so signed permutations of remaining orbit vertices preserve those pairs and induce the exact claimed integral normalizer module. Independently enumerated bars for weights (1,3,3),(2,2,2),(2,3,4,5) reproducing the displayed first two cases. r=0 and m=1 handled by augmentation convention; all-n proof is algebraic.
